label: late original-phase o/m/x/k input, gated by sequence-initial token (y,i,g,0,l,j,b,a)
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase (99% of mass), at positions t>=3 (mostly t=4-7), never at t<3, and is essentially silent in the copy phase. A weak tail fires on <DEL>. The input token matters most: o, m, x, k carry about 72% of mass (o is strongest), with smaller contributions from d, f, e, 3. Firing also depends on the earlier context. A sequence-initial token of y, i, g, 0, or l raises the rate several-fold (y gives 5x), and prior digits or v/l/c also help, which suggests accumulated hidden state. Top activations are o/m/x inputs in sequences that start with y. On its own the in_tok+position predicate reaches F1 0.33 with mass recall 0.71. Adding the first-token gate raises precision to about 0.6 (dev F1 0.48) but loses recall. Context dependence is graded and not fully captured. Does not fire in the copy phase, at t<3, or for most other input letters.
